Read the actual code (package.json, src/, scripts/, web/, assignments/, tsconfig.json, PLAN.md) and describe what is really there; do not invent features, commands or env vars. Do not modify any code. Only README.md may change (you may add a short .env.example only if the code really reads those variables), with one approved exception under cline-proof/ described in item 12; do not touch anything else under cline-proof/.

The README must include:
1. What HintLab is (one paragraph) and the safety promise: the tutor diagnoses and gives tiered hints but never writes the fix.
2. Prerequisites with exact versions and how to check/install them on macOS (Homebrew or Xcode Command Line Tools) and on Linux (Debian/Ubuntu apt, and a note for Fedora/dnf): Node.js 22 or newer (the Cline SDK requires it; npm included), python3, and a C compiler (gcc, or Apple clang via the gcc/cc shim on macOS), git. Mention any other tool the code or checks call (check the scripts, e.g. ps, lsof, curl).
3. ClinePass / provider setup: how to install the Cline CLI, how to authenticate it with ClinePass so that credentials land in ~/.cline (the exact CLI command(s) that exist in the installed CLI version; check its help output), how the server's Cline SDK picks those credentials up from ~/.cline with no API key in the repo, and how to use another provider instead if the code supports it. Never include any real token or secret.
4. Every environment variable the code reads (search the source for process.env), with default, meaning and example: e.g. PORT, HINTLAB_PROVIDER_ID, HINTLAB_MODEL_ID, timeouts, and any others actually present.
5. Install and run: clone, npm install, start (npm start and npm run dev), the URL to open, and a short demo walkthrough (pick an assignment, run, read the failing tests, watch the live feed, get hints at levels 1, 2 and 3, "all hints given").
6. Every npm script with what it does, and how to run the checks (typecheck, test:runner, check:agent, check:web, build) including which ones make real model calls, how long they take and what a pass looks like.
7. API reference: each endpoint, request body, response shape, status codes, and the SSE event types that reach the client (and the fact that model free text and reasoning are filtered out on the server).
8. Architecture: a diagram in text plus explanation of how the Cline SDK is used: ClineCore created once in local backend mode, start with interactive sessions and send for the next hint, toolPolicies disabling edit/write/network tools, requestToolApproval enforcing the run_commands allow-list (list the allowed command forms), the give_hint custom tool built with createTool and zod and passed through extraTools, subscribe events mapped to SSE, the server-side hint guard, and the sandboxed runner (temp dir per run, timeouts, process-group kill, minimal env, signal reporting, cleanup). Include the SDK quirks: Node 22+, moduleResolution Bundler, absolute paths for read_files, interactive start needed for send, run_commands runs on the host so the allow-list is the only protection.
9. Assignments: the format of assignments/<id>/tests.json and how to add a new assignment.
10. Troubleshooting: common failures (Node too old, missing gcc/python3, port in use, ClinePass not logged in or expired, model timeouts) and how to fix them.
11. Project layout tree and a short "How this was built" note: all code was written by the Cline CLI from the prompts in cline-proof/prompts, with session logs in cline-proof/sessions.

12. Repo cleanup and disclosure (approved by Prakhar): remove the folder cline-proof/reference/sdk-check/ from the repo using git rm -r on that folder (it stays in git history, which is fine; do not commit, I will commit). Keep cline-proof/reference/fixtures/ (the sample buggy programs are test data). Make sure nothing in the app, scripts, tsconfig or package.json references sdk-check (check with a search; if something does, report it rather than changing code). In the README add a short "Disclosure" section stating: example Cline SDK snippets were prepared before the sprint and used only as reference material for Cline; they were never imported by the app and were removed from the repo during the sprint; all app code was written by Cline during the sprint, as shown in cline-proof/ (prompts and session logs) and the Cline session history. Also state where the fixtures came from: the three sample buggy programs and their tests.json files in cline-proof/reference/fixtures/ were prepared before the sprint as test data, and were copied unchanged into assignments/.

Verify the README against reality before finishing: run every command it lists that is safe and quick (npm install, npm run typecheck, npm run test:runner, the CLI help for the auth command, and start the server on PORT=3200 and curl the health endpoint, then stop it by PID). Another tester may be using PORT=3100: never kill, signal or bind to processes on 3100, no broad pkill patterns. Do not run the real-model checks again unless needed. Report what you verified and anything in the README that you could not verify.</user_input>

1 | # HintLab
  2 | 
  3 | A debugging tutor for programming labs. A student pastes code and picks an
  4 | assignment; the server runs the code against the assignment's test cases in a
  5 | sandbox, then a Cline‑SDK agent diagnoses the failure and delivers **tiered
  6 | hints** (level 1 nudge → level 2 where to look → level 3 concept). It **never**
  7 | writes or reveals the fix.
  8 | 
  9 | This is **Step 04**: the full web UI, plus the server-side fixes from the Step 02
 10 | review — an explicit SSE event allow-list (no unguarded model output reaches the
 11 | browser), friendly errors, a hardened `run_tests` tool that replaces the host
 12 | `run_commands` shell, and a stricter allow-list/hint guard.
 13 | 
 14 | ## Requirements
 15 | 
 16 | - Node.js 22+ (verified on Node 24)
 17 | - Python 3 (`python3`) on PATH
 18 | - `gcc` on PATH (for the C assignment)
 19 | - A Cline CLI installation already authenticated with ClinePass (see
 20 |   [Agent credentials](#agent-credentials))
 21 | 
 22 | ## Install
 23 | 
 24 | ```sh
 25 | npm install
 26 | ```
 27 | 
 28 | ## Agent credentials (picked up from `~/.cline`)
 29 | 
 30 | The agent uses the same ClinePass provider/model as the Cline CLI:
 31 | 
 32 | - provider id: `cline-pass`
 33 | - model id: `cline-pass/deepseek-v4-pro`
 34 | 
 35 | The SDK does **not** need an API key in the repo or in env vars. In local
 36 | backend mode (`backendMode: "local"`), `ClineCore.start` resolves credentials
 37 | itself from the Cline CLI's config/data directory:
 38 | 
 39 | - `~/.cline/data/settings/providers.json` → the `cline-pass` entry, whose
 40 |   `settings.auth` holds the OAuth `accessToken`/`refreshToken`. When
 41 |   `config.apiKey` is omitted, the SDK's local runtime host resolves the
 42 |   provider's OAuth token from this file (refreshing it if expired) and injects
 43 |   it for the request.
 44 | 
 45 | Treat `~/.cline` as read-only: the server never writes to it, and never logs
 46 | any token/secret (it only ever prints provider/model names). You can override
 47 | the provider/model via env vars:
 48 | 
 49 | ```sh
 50 | HINTLAB_PROVIDER_ID=cline-pass HINTLAB_MODEL_ID=cline-pass/deepseek-v4-pro npm start
 51 | ```
 52 | 
 53 | ## Start the server
 54 | 
 55 | ```sh
 56 | npm run dev      # watch mode
 57 | npm start        # run once (tsx src/server.ts)
 58 | ```
 59 | 
 60 | The server listens on `http://localhost:3000` by default. Override with `PORT`:
 61 | 
 62 | ```sh
 63 | PORT=3200 npm start
 64 | ```
 65 | 
 66 | The web UI is served at `http://localhost:3200/` (plain HTML/CSS/vanilla JS, no
 67 | build step).
 68 | 
 69 | ### Using the UI
 70 | 
 71 | 1. Pick an assignment from the drop-down (it shows the statement and language and
 72 |    preloads the buggy starter code into the editor).
 73 | 2. Edit the code, then press **Run & get hint**.
 74 | 3. The test-results table appears (name, input, expected, got, PASS/FAIL with
 75 |    colour, plus timeout/signal/build errors), and the tutor's activity streams in
 76 |    live on the right.
 77 | 4. Hint cards appear as "Level 1: nudge" → "Level 2: where to look" → "Level 3:
 78 |    the concept". Press **Next hint** for the next level (it disables while the
 79 |    tutor is busy). Starting a new run resets everything.
 80 | 
 81 | ### Endpoints
 82 | 
 83 | | Method | Path                          | Description                                                      |
 84 | | ------ | ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
 85 | | GET    | `/`                           | Web UI (static `web/`)                                           |
 86 | | GET    | `/api/health`                 | Liveness check                                                   |
 87 | | GET    | `/api/assignments`            | List assignments (id, language, statement, starter code)         |
 88 | | POST   | `/api/session`                | Run a submission + start the agent. Body `{ assignmentId, code? }` |
 89 | | GET    | `/api/session/:id/stream`     | Server-Sent Events (replay + live) for the session               |
 90 | | POST   | `/api/session/:id/next-hint`  | Ask the agent for the next hint level (2, then 3)                |
 91 | 
 92 | `POST /api/session` runs the sandboxed runner, creates a session, starts the
 93 | agent in the background asking for a **level‑1** hint, and immediately returns
 94 | `{ sessionId, testResults }`. If `code` is omitted, the assignment's starter
 95 | program is used. Unknown session ids return `404`; `next-hint` returns `409`
 96 | while the agent is still busy, and `{ level: 3, status: "complete" }` once all
 97 | three levels have been delivered.
 98 | 
 99 | ```sh
100 | curl -s -X POST localhost:3200/api/session \
101 |   -H 'content-type: application/json' \
102 |   -d '{"assignmentId":"sum-of-list"}'
103 | ```
104 | 
105 | ### SSE event types
106 | 
107 | The stream only ever forwards a small **allow-list** of event types, each with a
108 | sanitised payload that can never contain the model's own text, reasoning, or raw
109 | SDK/stack-trace messages. Unguarded events (`agent_text`, `reasoning`, and tool
110 | inputs/outputs that carry model free text) are dropped at the server boundary and
111 | are never sent — including to late joiners via the replay buffer.
112 | 
113 | | Event            | What reaches the client                                       |
114 | | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
115 | | `test_results`   | Test results (name, input, expected, got, pass/fail, signal/timedOut, build error) — never `sandboxDir` |
116 | | `tool_call`      | Only `run_commands` (command), `read_files` (file name), or `run_tests` (test name) |
117 | | `tool_result`    | For `run_commands` a short trimmed output; for `run_tests` the pass/fail summary |
118 | | `approval`       | `allowed`/`denied` + the command (or tool name)               |
119 | | `hint`           | An accepted, guarded hint (`level`, `tag`, `text`)            |
120 | | `hint_status` / `hint_rejected` | Only a reason category (e.g. `wrong level`, `contained code`) — never the rejected text |
121 | | `status`         | Session status string only (`running`/`idle`/`complete`/`error`) |
122 | | `error`          | A short, friendly human line (no stack traces / raw SDK messages) |
123 | | `done`           | The agent finished a turn (reason only)                       |
124 | 
125 | A `: ping` heartbeat comment is sent every ~15s; buffered events are replayed to
126 | late-joining clients through the same filter.
127 | 
128 | ## Safety model
129 | 
130 | - The agent runs with `enableSpawnAgent: false` and `enableAgentTeams: false`.
131 | - All file-editing/network tools are disabled (`editor`, `apply_patch`,
132 |   `fetch_web_content`, `skills`, `ask_question`, `submit_and_exit` →
133 |   `{ enabled: false }`). `read_files`, `search_codebase`, `give_hint`, and
134 |   `run_tests` are auto-approved.
135 | - The built-in `run_commands` tool is **disabled** (`enabled: false`). Instead the
136 |   agent gets a custom `run_tests` tool that runs the student's code through the
137 |   hardened server runner (process-group kill, per-test timeouts, minimal env with
138 |   `HOME` set to the sandbox dir, signal reporting) — so student code run by the
139 |   agent can never read server env vars or the credentials in `~/.cline`.
140 | - `requestToolApproval` still denies everything that is not explicitly allowed, so
141 |   any command attempt is blocked and shown as an approval-denied line. The strict
142 |   regex allow-list in `src/allowlist.ts` is retained and unit-tested; it allows
143 |   only `python3 main.py`, the exact `gcc` build command, `./main`, a stdin
144 |   redirect from an `input-*.txt` file, and `cat` of `main.py`/`main.c`/`tests.json`
145 |   or an `input-*.txt` file. Any `$` (variable/command expansion) and any pipe
146 |   (`echo … | program`) are denied. Each test's input is written to its own
147 |   `input-<test-name>.txt` file in the workdir.
148 | - Hints can only be delivered through `give_hint`, and every hint is checked by
149 |   `src/hintGuard.ts` before it is stored/sent. A hint containing a fenced code
150 |   block, inline code, a one-line code expression (indexing/slicing, comparison or
151 |   arithmetic between identifiers, casts, calls, semicolons), or a rewritten
152 |   solution is rejected — while plain prose like "for x in the list" or "if the
153 |   list is empty" still passes.
154 | 
155 | ## Run the checks
156 | 
157 | ```sh
158 | npm run typecheck     # tsc --noEmit
159 | npm run test:runner   # sandboxed runner against the 3 buggy programs
160 | npm run check:agent   # end-to-end, REAL model call (starts a server on :3200)
161 | npm run check:web     # web UI + SSE contract (starts a server on :3200, stops by PID)
162 | ```
163 | 
164 | `test:runner` runs the sandboxed runner against all three buggy starter programs
165 | and asserts the exact expected pass/fail of every test, plus a correct solution
166 | for each assignment, an infinite-loop program (must time out), and a C program
167 | with a compile error (must report a build failure).
168 | 
169 | `check:agent` unit-tests the allow-list (including `$`-expansion and pipe
170 | injection attempts like `echo $HOME | python3 main.py`) and the hint guard (new
171 | one-line code expressions are rejected; prose like "for x in the list" passes),
172 | then starts the server on `PORT=3200`, posts a `sum-of-list` session, reads the
173 | SSE stream, and requests hints level 2 and 3. It asserts exactly one accepted hint
174 | per level, that no hint contains code, that **no `agent_text`/`reasoning` and no
175 | rejected hint text arrive over SSE**, that `run_commands` was never executed (and
176 | never approved), that `run_tests` was used (or tests were otherwise reported), and
177 | that no edit/write tool ran. It prints the hints verbatim, the distinct SSE event
178 | types, and the approval decisions, and exits non-zero on failure (overall timeout
179 | 8 minutes). It leaves no server running.
180 | 
181 | `check:web` starts the server on `PORT=3200`, fetches `/` (asserting the page
182 | loads with the app title and that `/app.js` and `/style.css` return 200), fetches
183 | `/api/assignments`, starts one real session on `is-palindrome` (or
184 | `average-marks`), reads the SSE stream until the level-1 hint (or a timeout), and
185 | asserts the event types contain no `agent_text`/`reasoning`. It prints the event
186 | types seen and the hint, then stops the server by PID. It leaves no server running.
187 | 
188 | ## Typecheck / build
189 | 
190 | ```sh
191 | npm run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
192 | npm run build       # tsc
193 | ```

1 | # HintLab — Build Plan
  2 | 
  3 | > A debugging tutor for programming labs. A student pastes code and picks an assignment; a Cline‑SDK agent runs it against the assignment's test cases in a temp sandbox, diagnoses the failure, and delivers **tiered hints** (level 1 nudge → level 2 where to look → level 3 concept). It must **never** write or reveal the fix.
  4 | 
  5 | ## 1. Architecture overview
  6 | 
  7 | ```
  8 | Browser (web/) ──POST /api/session──────────────► Express/TS server (src/)
  9 |    │            { assignmentId, code }              │
 10 |    │◄──────────── { sessionId, testResults } ───────┤
 11 |    │                                                ├─► Sandbox runner (src/runner.ts)
 12 |    │◄──GET /api/session/:id/stream (SSE)────────────┤     temp dir, build+run, trim, compare
 13 |    │      tool steps · results · hints · done/error │
 14 |    │                                                ├─► ClineCore agent (src/agent.ts)
 15 |    │◄──POST /api/session/:id/next-hint──────────────┤     toolPolicies + allow-list + give_hint
 16 |    │      (agent via cline.send)                    │
 17 |                                                     └─► assignments/<id>/tests.json (+starter)
 18 | ```
 19 | 
 20 | - **Server**: Express + TypeScript, ESM (`"type": "module"`), run via Node's built-in type stripping (`node --experimental-strip-types`) so there is no bundler/build step in the runtime path (matches how `sdk-check` was run).
 21 | - **Agent**: `@cline/sdk` 0.0.90 with `ClineCore`, `zod` 4.
 22 | - **Sandbox**: a fresh temp dir per session (e.g. `os.tmpdir()/hintlab-<id>`). The server's own runner executes the assignment's build/run commands there with timeouts.
 23 | - **Safety**: `editor`/`apply_patch` disabled; `run_commands` gated by a strict shell allow-list in `requestToolApproval`; hints only through a custom `give_hint` tool; `run_commands` runs on the host, so the allow-list + timeouts are the only protection.
 24 | 
 25 | ## 2. Repository layout (all new, outside `cline-proof/`)
 26 | 
 27 | ```
 28 | /Users/prakharagarwal/ClineHackathon
 29 | ├── PLAN.md
 30 | ├── package.json
 31 | ├── tsconfig.json
 32 | ├── .gitignore                # node_modules, dist, .env, *.tmp

 38 | ├── src/

 60 | ## 3. Environment & SDK quirk checklist
 61 | 
 62 | | # | Quirk | Where handled |
 63 | |---|-------|---------------|
 64 | | 1 | Node 22+ required (machine has v24.16.0) | `package.json` `engines` ≥22; document; no action needed beyond confirming |
 65 | | 2 | `moduleResolution: "Bundler"` + `module: "ESNext"` | `tsconfig.json` (copy the sdk-check tsconfig: `target ES2022`, `strict`, `skipLibCheck`, `noEmit`, `allowImportingTsExtensions`, `types:["node"]`) |
 66 | | 3 | `read_files` needs absolute paths | prompt builder injects `path.resolve(sandboxDir)` for code + tests |
 67 | | 4 | `send()` follow-up only works with `interactive: true` | `agent.ts` always calls `start({ interactive: true, … })` |
 68 | | 5 | `run_commands` runs on the host | allow-list in `requestToolApproval`; server runner uses timeouts; allow-list regexes forbid shell metacharacters & `/` outside the fixed prefix |
 69 | 
 70 | ## 4. Fixture analysis — expected test results
 71 | 
 72 | **sum-of-list** (`main.py`) — bug: `for i in range(1, len(nums))` starts at index 1, skipping `nums[0]`.
 73 | | test | input | expected | buggy got | result |
 74 | |---|---|---|---|---|
 75 | | basic | `1 2 3` | `6` | `5` | ❌ FAIL |
 76 | | single | `7` | `7` | `0` | ❌ FAIL |
 77 | | negatives | `-4 10 -1` | `5` | `9` | ❌ FAIL |
 78 | | first-only-big | `100 1` | `101` | `1` | ❌ FAIL |
 79 | 
 80 | → **0/4 pass.** Root cause: off-by-one (loop should start at `range(0, len(nums))`).
 81 | 
 82 | **is-palindrome** (`main.py`) — bug: compares raw string, never ignores case/spaces.
 83 | | test | input | expected | buggy got | result |
 84 | |---|---|---|---|---|
 85 | | simple | `racecar` | `YES` | `YES` | ✅ PASS |

 92 | `POST /api/session` runs the sandboxed runner, creates a session, starts the
 93 | agent in the background asking for a **level‑1** hint, and immediately returns
 94 | `{ sessionId, testResults }`. If `code` is omitted, the assignment's starter
 95 | program is used. Unknown session ids return `404`; `next-hint` returns `409`
 96 | while the agent is still busy, and `{ level: 3, status: "complete" }` once all
 97 | three levels have been delivered.
 98 | 
 99 | ```sh
100 | curl -s -X POST localhost:3200/api/session \
101 |   -H 'content-type: application/json' \
102 |   -d '{"assignmentId":"sum-of-list"}'
103 | ```
104 | 
105 | ### SSE event types
106 | 
107 | The stream only ever forwards a small **allow-list** of event types, each with a
108 | sanitised payload that can never contain the model's own text, reasoning, or raw
109 | SDK/stack-trace messages. Unguarded events (`agent_text`, `reasoning`, and tool
110 | inputs/outputs that carry model free text) are dropped at the server boundary and
111 | are never sent — including to late joiners via the replay buffer.
112 | 
113 | | Event            | What reaches the client                                       |
114 | | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
115 | | `test_results`   | Test results (name, input, expected, got, pass/fail, signal/timedOut, build error) — never `sandboxDir` |
116 | | `tool_call`      | Only `run_commands` (command), `read_files` (file name), or `run_tests` (test name) |
117 | | `tool_result`    | For `run_commands` a short trimmed output; for `run_tests` the pass/fail summary |
118 | | `approval`       | `allowed`/`denied` + the command (or tool name)               |
119 | | `hint`           | An accepted, guarded hint (`level`, `tag`, `text`)            |
120 | | `hint_status` / `hint_rejected` | Only a reason category (e.g. `wrong level`, `contained code`) — never the rejected text |
121 | | `status`         | Session status string only (`running`/`idle`/`complete`/`error`) |
122 | | `error`          | A short, friendly human line (no stack traces / raw SDK messages) |
123 | | `done`           | The agent finished a turn (reason only)                       |
124 | 
125 | A `: ping` heartbeat comment is sent every ~15s; buffered events are replayed to
126 | late-joining clients through the same filter.

128 | ## Safety model
129 | 
130 | - The agent runs with `enableSpawnAgent: false` and `enableAgentTeams: false`.
131 | - All file-editing/network tools are disabled (`editor`, `apply_patch`,
132 |   `fetch_web_content`, `skills`, `ask_question`, `submit_and_exit` →
133 |   `{ enabled: false }`). `read_files`, `search_codebase`, `give_hint`, and
134 |   `run_tests` are auto-approved.
135 | - The built-in `run_commands` tool is **disabled** (`enabled: false`). Instead the
136 |   agent gets a custom `run_tests` tool that runs the student's code through the
137 |   hardened server runner (process-group kill, per-test timeouts, minimal env with
138 |   `HOME` set to the sandbox dir, signal reporting) — so student code run by the
139 |   agent can never read server env vars or the credentials in `~/.cline`.
140 | - `requestToolApproval` still denies everything that is not explicitly allowed, so
141 |   any command attempt is blocked and shown as an approval-denied line. The strict
142 |   regex allow-list in `src/allowlist.ts` is retained and unit-tested; it allows
143 |   only `python3 main.py`, the exact `gcc` build command, `./main`, a stdin
144 |   redirect from an `input-*.txt` file, and `cat` of `main.py`/`main.c`/`tests.json`
145 |   or an `input-*.txt` file. Any `$` (variable/command expansion) and any pipe
146 |   (`echo … | program`) are denied. Each test's input is written to its own
147 |   `input-<test-name>.txt` file in the workdir.
148 | - Hints can only be delivered through `give_hint`, and every hint is checked by
149 |   `src/hintGuard.ts` before it is stored/sent. A hint containing a fenced code
150 |   block, inline code, a one-line code expression (indexing/slicing, comparison or
151 |   arithmetic between identifiers, casts, calls, semicolons), or a rewritten
152 |   solution is rejected — while plain prose like "for x in the list" or "if the
153 |   list is empty" still passes.

| test | input | expected | buggy got | result |

**is-palindrome** (`main.py`) — bug: compares raw string, never ignores case/spaces.
| test | input | expected | buggy got | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| simple | `racecar` | `YES` | `YES` | ✅ PASS |
| not | `hello` | `NO` | `NO` | ✅ PASS |
| mixed-case | `Madam` | `YES` | `NO` | ❌ FAIL |
| spaces | `never odd or even` | `YES` | `NO` | ❌ FAIL |

→ **2/4 pass.** Root cause: missing normalization (lowercase + strip spaces before reversing).

**average-marks** (`main.c`) — bug: `float avg = sum / n;` is integer division.
| test | input | expected | buggy got | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| even | `2\n10 20` | `15.00` | `15.00` | ✅ PASS |
| fraction | `3\n1 2 2` | `1.67` | `1.00` | ❌ FAIL |
| half | `2\n3 4` | `3.50` | `3.00` | ❌ FAIL |

→ **1/3 pass.** Root cause: integer truncation (needs `(float)sum / n`).

# HintLab

HintLab is a debugging tutor for programming labs. A student picks an assignment (or pastes their own program), the server runs the code against the assignment's test cases in a sandboxed temporary directory, and then a Cline-SDK agent diagnoses the failures and delivers **tiered hints** — level 1 (a conceptual nudge), level 2 (where to look), level 3 (the underlying concept) — streamed live to the browser. It is built as an Express + TypeScript server (ESM), a vanilla-JS web UI, and an agent built on `@cline/sdk`'s `ClineCore`.

**Safety promise:** the tutor only diagnoses and hints. It **never** writes or reveals the fix: file-editing and network tools are disabled at the SDK policy level, the shell command tool is replaced by a hardened `run_tests` tool and gated by a strict allow-list, and every hint is checked by a server-side guard before it reaches the student. Model free text and reasoning are filtered out on the server, so only a small allow-list of sanitised events ever reaches the browser.

## 2. Cline CLI + ClinePass (provider credentials)

HintLab does **not** ship or read an API key. In local backend mode the SDK resolves credentials itself from the Cline CLI's config directory (`~/.cline`), so the only setup step is to install the CLI and authenticate it with ClinePass once.

1. Install the CLI (installs the `cline` binary):
   ```sh
   npm install -g cline
   cline --version      # verified on 3.0.68
   ```
2. Authenticate with ClinePass. `cline auth` has a positional provider shorthand and flags:
   ```sh
   cline auth --help
   # Usage: cline auth [options] [provider]
   #   provider              Provider id (positional shorthand for -p)
   #   -p, --provider <id>   Provider ID
   #   -k, --apikey <key>    API key
   #   -m, --modelid <id>    Model ID
   #   -b, --baseurl <url>   Base URL

   cline auth cline-pass -m cline-pass/deepseek-v4-pro
   # (or: cline auth -p cline-pass -m cline-pass/deepseek-v4-pro)
   ```
   This runs the ClinePass OAuth login flow (browser/device flow — follow the prompts). On success the CLI writes the ClinePass credentials to:
   ```
   ~/.cline/data/settings/providers.json   →  providers["cline-pass"].settings.auth
       { accessToken, refreshToken, expiresAt, accountId, metadata }
   ```
   Confirm with `cline config`.

3. How the server picks it up: `src/config.ts` defaults `HINTLAB_PROVIDER_ID=cline-pass` and `HINTLAB_MODEL_ID=cline-pass/deepseek-v4-pro`. `src/agent.ts` creates `ClineCore.create({ clientName: "hintlab", backendMode: "local" })` and passes those ids (and no API key) to `cline.start(...)`. In local mode the SDK's runtime host reads the provider's OAuth token from `~/.cline/data/settings/providers.json`, refreshes it if expired, and injects it for the request. Treat `~/.cline` as read-only: the server never writes to it and never logs any token (it only ever prints provider/model names).

4. Using a different provider: the code supports any provider the CLI has credentials for, via env overrides. Authenticate it with the CLI first (so its credentials land in `~/.cline`), then run:
   ```sh
   HINTLAB_PROVIDER_ID=anthropic HINTLAB_MODEL_ID=claude-sonnet-4-5 npm start
   ```
   (There is no `API_KEY` env var and no `config.apiKey`; the only supported credential source is `~/.cline`.)

There is **no `.env` file and no dotenv loading** — `src/config.ts` reads `process.env` directly. Set them inline (`VAR=value npm start`) or export them. Everything has a safe default.

| `PORT` | `3000` | HTTP port the server listens on |
| `RUN_TIMEOUT_MS` | `5000` | Per-test run timeout (ms) |
| `BUILD_TIMEOUT_MS` | `15000` | Build (gcc) timeout (ms) |
| `MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES` | `1048576` (1 MiB) | Max captured stdout/stderr bytes per process |

## 5. npm scripts and checks

| Script | Command | What it does |
|--------|---------|--------------|
| `npm start` | `tsx src/server.ts` | Run the server once |
| `npm run dev` | `tsx watch src/server.ts` | Run in watch mode (restarts on change) |
| `npm run build` | `tsc` | Type-check + emit JS to `dist/` (per `tsconfig.json`) |
| `npm run typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit` | Type-check only, no output |
| `npm run test:runner` | `tsx scripts/check-runner.ts` | Sandboxed runner checks — **no model call** |
| `npm run check:agent` | `tsx scripts/check-agent.ts` | Allow-list + hint-guard unit tests + a **real model** e2e on `sum-of-list` |
| `npm run check:web` | `tsx scripts/check-web.ts` | Static UI + SSE contract + a **real model** session |

What each check does and what a pass looks like:

- **`npm run typecheck`** — `tsc --noEmit` across `src/` and `scripts/`. No network, no model. Pass = exit 0, no output.
- **`npm run test:runner`** — runs the sandboxed runner against all three buggy starters and asserts the exact pass/fail of every test (sum-of-list 0/4, is-palindrome 2/4, average-marks 1/3), plus a correct solution for each assignment, an infinite-loop program (must time out), a C compile error (must report a build failure), a segfault (must report `SIGSEGV`), process-group kill (no stray `sleep` left behind, checked with `pgrep`), minimal-env (no leak of server env), and temp-dir cleanup. **No model call.** Takes a few seconds. Pass = `ALL CHECKS PASSED`, exit 0.
- **`npm run check:agent`** — first unit-tests the run_commands allow-list (including `$`-expansion and pipe injection) and the hint guard, then starts a server on **`PORT=3200`**, posts a `sum-of-list` session, reads the SSE stream, and requests hints at levels 2 and 3. It asserts exactly one accepted hint per level, that no hint contains code, that **no `agent_text`/`reasoning` and no rejected-hint text reach SSE**, that `run_commands` was never executed or approved, that `run_tests` was used (or results reported), and that no edit/write tool ran. **Makes real model calls** (needs the ClinePass login above). Overall timeout 8 minutes; prints the hints verbatim, the distinct SSE event types, and approval decisions; exits non-zero on failure. Leaves no server running.
- **`npm run check:web`** — starts the server on **`PORT=3200`**, fetches `/` (asserts the page title/tagline and that `/app.js` + `/style.css` return 200), fetches `/api/assignments`, starts one real session on `is-palindrome` (or `average-marks`), reads the SSE stream until the level-1 hint (or a timeout), and asserts the event types contain no `agent_text`/`reasoning`. **Makes real model calls.** Stops the server by PID; leaves nothing running.

> The checks hard-code port **3200** and start/stop their own server; they don't touch `PORT=3000`. `typecheck` and `test:runner` are the only checks that need no ClinePass login.

## 6. API reference

Base URL `http://localhost:3000` (or your `PORT`).

### `GET /api/health`
- Response `200`: `{ "status": "ok" }`

### `GET /api/assignments`
- Response `200`: array of `{ id, language, statement, starterCode }` for each discovered assignment.

### `POST /api/session`
Run a submission and start a background level-1 agent turn.
- Request body: `{ "assignmentId": "sum-of-list", "code": "…" }` (`code` optional — omitted/empty/`null` uses the starter code).
- Response `200`: `{ "sessionId": "<uuid>", "testResults": { assignmentId, build, tests[], passed, failed, total } }` (the `testResults` are the **sanitised** shape below — no `sandboxDir`, trimmed `stderr`).
- Errors: `400` (body not an object, bad/missing `assignmentId`, `code` not a string), `404` (`assignmentId` unknown), `500` (internal error).

### `GET /api/session/:id/stream`
Server-Sent Events. `200`/`text/event-stream`; `404` if unknown session. Replays buffered events then streams live ones; sends `: ping` heartbeats.

### `POST /api/session/:id/next-hint`
Ask for the next hint level (2, then 3).
- Response `200`: `{ "level": 2, "status": "running" }` (the hint itself arrives over SSE). After level 3 it returns `{ "level": 3, "status": "complete", "message": "All three hint levels have already been delivered." }`.
- Errors: `404` unknown session, `409` agent still busy.

### Static
`GET /` and `web/` assets are served with `express.static`.

### SSE event types that reach the client
Only these are ever forwarded (everything else — including the model's free text and reasoning — is dropped by `src/eventFilter.ts`):

| Event | Payload |
|-------|---------|
| `test_results` | `{ assignmentId, build: { ok, timedOut, signal, stderr } | null, tests: [{ name, input, expected, got, stderr, exitCode, signal, timedOut, passed }], passed, failed, total }` |
| `tool_call` | `run_commands` → `{ toolName, command }`; `read_files` → `{ toolName, file }`; `run_tests` → `{ toolName, testName }` |
| `tool_result` | `run_commands` → `{ toolName, output }`; `run_tests` → `{ toolName, passed, failed, total, build, tests[] }` (read_files results are **dropped** — they'd leak the student's code) |
| `approval` | `{ toolName, command, allowed, reason? }` (in HintLab `allowed` is always `false`) |
| `hint` | `{ level, tag, text }` |
| `hint_status` | `{ level, reason }` (fixed category) |
| `hint_rejected` | `{ level, reason }` where reason ∈ `"wrong level" | "empty hint" | "contained code"` (never the rejected text) |
| `status` | `{ status }` (e.g. `created`, `running`, `idle`, `complete`, `error`) |
| `error` | `{ message }` (a short friendly message — never a stack trace or SDK text) |
| `done` | `{ reason }` |

**Filtering:** raw agent events (`agent_text`, `reasoning`, unguarded tool output) are recorded server-side for debugging but never streamed; `filterEvent` applies the allow-list + sanitisation to both live events and replayed history.

## 7. Architecture

```
 Browser (web/index.html + app.js — vanilla JS, EventSource)
   │  POST /api/session  { assignmentId, code }
   ▼
 Express + TS server (src/app.ts, src/server.ts)          ESM, run via tsx
   │
   ├─ runAssignment(...,{cleanup:false}) ──► sandbox runner (src/runner.ts)
   │     fresh temp dir os.tmpdir()/hintlab-<uuid>
   │     writes main.py/main.c + tests.json + input-<name>.txt
   │     build (gcc) / run (python3|./main) with per-test timeout,
   │     process-group kill, minimal env (PATH, HOME=sandbox, LANG)
   │
   ├─ startSession / nextHint ──► ClineCore agent (src/agent.ts)
   │     ClineCore.create({ clientName:"hintlab", backendMode:"local" })  (once, lazy)
   │     cline.start({ interactive:true, prompt, config:{sessionId, providerId, modelId,
   │                   temperature:0, systemPrompt, cwd, workspaceRoot, enableTools,
   │                   enableSpawnAgent:false, enableAgentTeams:false, extraTools}, toolPolicies, capabilities })
   │     cline.send({ sessionId, prompt })  for next hint
   │     cline.subscribe(handleCoreEvent)   →  mapped to SSE events
   │     give_hint (createTool + zod)  +  run_tests (createTool + zod)  via extraTools
   │
   ├─ GET  /api/session/:id/stream  (SSE)  ◄── eventFilter.ts allow-list + sanitisation
   └─ POST /api/session/:id/next-hint
```

### How the SDK is used
- **One `ClineCore`**, created lazily in **local backend mode** (`ClineCore.create({ clientName: "hintlab", backendMode: "local" })`) and subscribed once; reused across sessions.
- **Start + send:** the first turn is `cline.start({ interactive: true, prompt, config: {...}, toolPolicies, capabilities })`; follow-up hint levels use `cline.send({ sessionId, prompt })`.
- **Tool policies** (`toolPolicies()` in `src/agent.ts`): `run_commands`, `editor`, `apply_patch`, `fetch_web_content`, `skills`, `ask_question`, `submit_and_exit` are `{ enabled: false }`; `read_files`, `search_codebase`, `give_hint`, `run_tests` are auto-approved.
- **Approval** (`capabilities().requestToolApproval`): returns `{ approved: false }` for everything, so any attempt is blocked and surfaced as an `approval` (denied) event. This is the gate in front of `run_commands` (defence-in-depth on top of the policy disable).
- **`run_commands` allow-list** (`src/allowlist.ts`): rejects any command containing `; && || ` $ | > & newline CR * ?`, then requires an exact match of the whitelist — only `python3 main.py`, `python3 main.py < input-*.txt`, `gcc -Wall -O0 main.c -o main`, `./main`, `./main < input-*.txt`, and `cat (main.py|main.c|tests.json|input-*.txt)`. Since `run_commands` runs **on the host**, this allow-list (plus the disabled policy) is the only protection between the model and an arbitrary shell.
- **Custom tools:** `give_hint` and `run_tests` are built with `createTool(...)` + zod schemas and passed through `config.extraTools`. `give_hint` is the only hint sink (server-side guard runs inside its `execute`); `run_tests` runs student code through the hardened server runner instead of the host shell.
- **Events:** `cline.subscribe(handleCoreEvent)` maps SDK `agent_event`s (tool starts/ends, done, error) and `status`/`ended` to the SSE allow-list; model text/reasoning are dropped.
- **Hint guard** (`src/hintGuard.ts`): rejects a hint containing a fenced code block, inline code beyond a short identifier, or any line that looks like source code (control flow, function calls, assignments, casts, indexing/slicing, comparisons, trailing semicolons). A rejected hint becomes a tool error so the model rephrases.
- **Sandboxed runner** (`src/runner.ts`): a fresh temp dir per run, per-test timeouts, `detached:true` + process-group `SIGKILL` to reap children, a minimal env (`PATH`, `HOME`=sandbox, `LANG`) so student code can't see server env or `~/.cline`, signal reporting (`SIGSEGV` etc.), and cleanup of the temp dir (except the agent's workdir, removed later at TTL).

### SDK quirks worth knowing
1. **Node 22+** — the SDK and `package.json` `engines` require it.
2. **`moduleResolution: "Bundler"`** (with `module: "ESNext"`) — required by the SDK's type exports (`tsconfig.json`).
3. **`read_files` needs absolute paths** — the prompt builder injects `path.resolve(sandboxDir, ...)`.
4. **`send()` follow-ups only work after an `interactive: true` `start()`** — `src/agent.ts` always starts interactively.
5. **`run_commands` runs on the host** — so the allow-list + disabled policy is the only protection; that's why the agent's own test execution goes through the custom `run_tests` tool instead.

## 8. Assignments

Each assignment is a directory under `assignments/<id>/` containing a `tests.json` and a starter source file. `id` is the directory name and must be a "plain slug" (`^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$` — lowercase letters/digits separated by single hyphens).

`tests.json` shape:
```json
{
  "assignmentId": "sum-of-list",
  "language": "python",
  "statement": "Read space-separated integers on one line and print their sum.",
  "run": "python3 main.py",
  "build": "gcc -Wall -O0 main.c -o main",
  "tests": [
    { "name": "basic", "input": "1 2 3\n", "expected": "6" }
  ]
}
```
- `language`: `"python"` or `"c"`.
- `run`: the command to run the program; `build` (optional, C only): the compile command.
- Each test: `name` (unique), `input` (fed to stdin verbatim), `expected` (compared to trimmed stdout).

The starter file is `main.py` (Python) or `main.c` (C), loaded as the editor's pre-filled "buggy" code. To add an assignment, create `assignments/<id>/{tests.json, main.py|main.c}`; `listAssignments()` discovers it automatically (no restart needed to list, and the runner reads it fresh per session).

## 9. Troubleshooting

- **`node` too old / `npm install` fails** — the SDK needs Node ≥ 22. `node --version`; install Node 22+ (see §1). 
- **Missing `gcc` or `python3`** — `test:runner` and the C assignment need them. `gcc --version`, `python3 --version`. macOS: `xcode-select --install`. Debian/Ubuntu: `sudo apt install -y build-essential python3`. Fedora: `sudo dnf install -y gcc python3`.
- **`EADDRINUSE` / "port already in use"** — another process holds the port. Use `PORT=3200 npm start` or find the pid: `lsof -i :3000` (macOS) / `ss -ltnp` (Linux), then `kill <pid>`. (The bundled checks use `PORT=3200` and manage their own server.)
- **"Tutor timed out" / no hint appears** — a model call is slow or ClinePass is expired. Check the feed and server log. If ClinePass expired, re-auth: `cline auth cline-pass`. The per-turn timeout is `AGENT_TURN_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 5 min).
- **ClinePass not logged in / expired** — `cline config` shows the current provider; re-run `cline auth cline-pass`. Without valid credentials the agent turns will fail with an error event.
- **`cline: command not found`** — the CLI isn't on PATH; `npm install -g cline` (check `npm config get prefix` is on PATH, e.g. `~/.npm-global/bin`).
- **Agent turns error with a hint-rejection** — normal: the model tried a code-bearing hint and the guard made it rephrase; you'll see `hint_rejected` in the feed.

# HintLab

HintLab is a debugging tutor for programming labs. A student picks an assignment (or
pastes their own program), the server runs the code against the assignment's test cases
in a sandboxed temporary directory, and then a Cline-SDK agent diagnoses the failures
and delivers **tiered hints** — level 1 (a conceptual nudge), level 2 (where to look),

shell command tool is replaced by a hardened `run_tests` tool and gated by a strict
allow-list, and every hint is checked by a server-side guard before it reaches the
student. Model free text and reasoning are filtered out on the server, so only a small
allow-list of sanitised events ever reaches the browser.

## 2. Cline CLI + ClinePass (provider credentials)

HintLab does **not** ship or read an API key. In local backend mode the SDK resolves
credentials itself from the Cline CLI's config directory (`~/.cline`), so the only setup
step is to install the CLI and authenticate it with ClinePass once.

1. Install the CLI (installs the `cline` binary):

   ```sh
   npm install -g cline
   cline --version      # verified on 3.0.68
   ```

2. Authenticate with ClinePass. `cline auth` takes a positional provider shorthand and
   flags (`-p/--provider`, `-k/--apikey`, `-m/--modelid`, `-b/--baseurl`):

   ```sh
   cline auth --help
   # Usage: cline auth [options] [provider]
   #   provider              Provider id (positional shorthand for -p)
   #   -p, --provider <id>   Provider ID
   #   -k, --apikey <key>    API key
   #   -m, --modelid <id>    Model ID
   #   -b, --baseurl <url>   Base URL

   cline auth cline-pass -m cline-pass/deepseek-v4-pro
   # (equivalent: cline auth -p cline-pass -m cline-pass/deepseek-v4-pro)
   ```

   This runs the ClinePass OAuth login flow (follow the prompts). On success the CLI
   writes the ClinePass credentials to:

   ```
   ~/.cline/data/settings/providers.json   ->   providers["cline-pass"].settings.auth
       { accessToken, refreshToken, expiresAt, accountId, metadata }
   ```

   Confirm with `cline config`.

3. **How the server picks them up:** `src/config.ts` defaults
   `HINTLAB_PROVIDER_ID=cline-pass` and `HINTLAB_MODEL_ID=cline-pass/deepseek-v4-pro`.
   `src/agent.ts` creates `ClineCore.create({ clientName: "hintlab", backendMode: "local" })`
   and passes those ids (and **no** API key) to `cline.start(...)`. In local mode the SDK's
   runtime host reads the provider's OAuth token from
   `~/.cline/data/settings/providers.json`, refreshes it if expired, and injects it for the
   request. Treat `~/.cline` as read-only: the server never writes to it and never logs any
   token (it only ever prints provider/model names).

4. **Using a different provider:** the code supports any provider the CLI has credentials
   for, via env overrides. Authenticate that provider with the CLI first (so its
   credentials land in `~/.cline`), then run:

   ```sh
   HINTLAB_PROVIDER_ID=anthropic HINTLAB_MODEL_ID=claude-sonnet-4-5 npm start
   ```

   There is no `API_KEY` env var and no `config.apiKey`; the only supported credential
   source is `~/.cline`.

## 3. Environment variables

There is **no `.env` file and no dotenv loading** — `src/config.ts` reads `process.env`
directly. Set them inline (`VAR=value npm start`) or export them. Every variable has a
safe default.

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `PORT` | `3000` | HTTP port the server listens on |
| `RUN_TIMEOUT_MS` | `5000` | Per-test run timeout (ms) |
| `BUILD_TIMEOUT_MS` | `15000` | Build (`gcc`) timeout (ms) |
| `MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES` | `1048576` (1 MiB) | Max captured stdout/stderr bytes per process |
| `HINTLAB_PROVIDER_ID` | `cline-pass` | Provider id passed to `ClineCore` |
| `HINTLAB_MODEL_ID` | `cline-pass/deepseek-v4-pro` | Model id passed to `ClineCore` |
| `AGENT_TURN_TIMEOUT_MS` | `300000` (5 min) | Max time an agent turn (`start`/`send`) may run |
| `SESSION_TTL_MS` | `1800000` (30 min) | Idle session lifetime before cleanup |
| `SESSION_CLEANUP_INTERVAL_MS` | `60000` (1 min) | How often the cleanup loop runs |
| `HEARTBEAT_MS` | `15000` | SSE keep-alive heartbeat interval |

(Internally the runner also reads `process.env.PATH` to build the minimal environment it
hands to student code — that's the OS `PATH`, not an app setting.)

## 4. Install and run

```sh
git clone <repo-url> hintlab && cd hintlab
npm install

npm start        # run once (tsx src/server.ts)
npm run dev      # watch mode (tsx watch src/server.ts)

## 5. npm scripts and checks

| Script | Command | What it does |
|--------|---------|--------------|
| `npm start` | `tsx src/server.ts` | Run the server once |
| `npm run dev` | `tsx watch src/server.ts` | Run in watch mode (restarts on change) |
| `npm run build` | `tsc` | Type-check and emit JS to `dist/` (per `tsconfig.json`) |
| `npm run typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit` | Type-check only, no output |
| `npm run test:runner` | `tsx scripts/check-runner.ts` | Sandboxed runner checks — **no model call** |
| `npm run check:agent` | `tsx scripts/check-agent.ts` | Allow-list + hint-guard unit tests + a **real model** e2e on `sum-of-list` |
| `npm run check:web` | `tsx scripts/check-web.ts` | Static UI + SSE contract + a **real model** session |

- **`npm run typecheck`** — `tsc --noEmit` across `src/` and `scripts/`. No network, no model.
  Pass = exit 0 with no output. A few seconds.
- **`npm run test:runner`** — runs the sandboxed runner against all three buggy starters and
  asserts the exact pass/fail of every test (sum-of-list 0/4, is-palindrome 2/4,
  average-marks 1/3), plus a correct solution for each assignment, an infinite-loop program
  (must time out), a C compile error (must report a build failure), a segfault (must report
  `SIGSEGV`), process-group kill (no stray `sleep` left behind, checked with `pgrep`),
  minimal-env (server env does not leak), and temp-dir cleanup. **No model call.** A few
  seconds. Pass = `ALL CHECKS PASSED`, exit 0.
- **`npm run check:agent`** — first unit-tests the run_commands allow-list (including
  `$`-expansion and pipe injection) and the hint guard; then it starts a server on
  **`PORT=3200`**, posts a `sum-of-list` session, reads the SSE stream, and requests hints
  at levels 2 and 3. It asserts exactly one accepted hint per level, that no hint contains
  code, that **no `agent_text`/`reasoning` and no rejected-hint text reach SSE**, that
  `run_commands` was never executed or approved, that `run_tests` was used (or results
  otherwise reported), and that no edit/write tool ran. **Makes real model calls** (needs the
  ClinePass login above). Overall timeout 8 minutes; prints the hints verbatim, the distinct
  SSE event types, and the approval decisions; exits non-zero on failure. Leaves no server
  running.
- **`npm run check:web`** — starts the server on **`PORT=3200`**, fetches `/` (asserts the
  page title/tagline and that `/app.js` + `/style.css` return 200), fetches
  `/api/assignments`, starts one real session on `is-palindrome` (or `average-marks`), reads
  the SSE stream until the level-1 hint (or a timeout), and asserts the event types contain
  no `agent_text`/`reasoning`. **Makes real model calls.** Stops the server by PID; leaves
  nothing running.

> The checks hard-code port **3200** and start/stop their own server; they never touch
> `PORT=3000`. `typecheck` and `test:runner` are the only checks that need no ClinePass login.

## 6. API reference

Base URL `http://localhost:3000` (or your `PORT`).

### `GET /api/health`
- `200` → `{ "status": "ok" }`

### `GET /api/assignments`
- `200` → array of `{ id, language, statement, starterCode }` for each discovered assignment.

### `POST /api/session`
Run a submission and start a background level-1 agent turn.
- Request body: `{ "assignmentId": "sum-of-list", "code": "…" }` — `code` is optional
  (omitted / empty / `null` uses the starter code).
- `200` → `{ "sessionId": "<uuid>", "testResults": { assignmentId, build, tests[], passed, failed, total } }`
  (`testResults` is the sanitised shape below — no `sandboxDir`, trimmed `stderr`).
- Errors: `400` (body not an object, missing/bad `assignmentId`, `code` not a string),
  `404` (unknown `assignmentId`), `500` (internal error).

### `GET /api/session/:id/stream`
Server-Sent Events. `200`/`text/event-stream`; `404` if the session is unknown. Replays the
buffered events, then streams live ones, with `: ping` heartbeats.

### `POST /api/session/:id/next-hint`
Ask for the next hint level (2, then 3).
- `200` → `{ "level": 2, "status": "idle" }` — the hint itself arrives over SSE. After all
  three hints: `{ "level": 3, "status": "complete", "message": "All three hint levels have already been delivered." }`.
- Errors: `404` unknown session, `409` agent still busy.

### Static
`GET /` and the `web/` assets are served with `express.static`.

### SSE event types that reach the client

Only the types below are ever forwarded; everything else (including the model's free text
and reasoning) is dropped by `src/eventFilter.ts`.

| Event | Payload |
|-------|---------|
| `test_results` | `{ assignmentId, build: { ok, timedOut, signal, stderr } \| null, tests: [{ name, input, expected, got, stderr, exitCode, signal, timedOut, passed }], passed, failed, total }` |
| `tool_call` | `run_commands` → `{ toolName, command }`; `read_files` → `{ toolName, file }`; `run_tests` → `{ toolName, testName }` |
| `tool_result` | `run_commands` → `{ toolName, output }`; `run_tests` → `{ toolName, passed, failed, total, build, tests[] }` (`read_files` results are dropped — they would leak the student's code) |
| `approval` | `{ toolName, command, allowed, reason? }` (in HintLab `allowed` is always `false`) |
| `hint` | `{ level, tag, text }` |
| `hint_rejected` | `{ level, reason }` with `reason` ∈ `"wrong level" \| "empty hint" \| "contained code"` (never the rejected text) |
| `hint_status` | whitelisted (reserved); the server currently emits `hint_rejected` instead |
| `status` | `{ status }` — `created`, `running`, `idle`, `complete`, `error` |
| `error` | `{ message }` — a short friendly line, never a stack trace or SDK text |
| `done` | `{ reason }` |

**Filtering:** raw agent events (`agent_text`, `reasoning`, unguarded tool output) are
recorded server-side for debugging but never streamed; `filterEvent` applies the allow-list
and sanitisation to both live events and the replayed history, so late joiners get the same
contract.
HL_EOF

## 7. Architecture

```
 Browser (web/index.html + app.js — vanilla JS, EventSource)
   │  POST /api/session  { assignmentId, code }
   ▼
 Express + TS server (src/app.ts, src/server.ts)          ESM, run via tsx
   │
   ├─ runAssignment(...,{cleanup:false}) ──► sandbox runner (src/runner.ts)
   │     fresh temp dir os.tmpdir()/hintlab-<uuid>
   │     writes main.py/main.c + tests.json + input-<name>.txt
   │     build (gcc) / run (python3|./main) with per-test timeout,
   │     process-group kill, minimal env (PATH, HOME=sandbox, LANG)
   │
   ├─ startSession / nextHint ──► ClineCore agent (src/agent.ts)
   │     ClineCore.create({ clientName:"hintlab", backendMode:"local" })   (once, lazy)
   │     cline.start({ interactive:true, prompt, config:{sessionId, providerId, modelId,
   │                   temperature:0, systemPrompt, cwd, workspaceRoot, enableTools,
   │                   enableSpawnAgent:false, enableAgentTeams:false, extraTools},
   │                   toolPolicies, capabilities })
   │     cline.send({ sessionId, prompt })   for the next hint
   │     cline.subscribe(handleCoreEvent)    ->  mapped to SSE events
   │     give_hint (createTool + zod)  +  run_tests (createTool + zod)  via extraTools
   │
   ├─ GET  /api/session/:id/stream  (SSE)  ◄── eventFilter.ts allow-list + sanitisation
   └─ POST /api/session/:id/next-hint
```

### How the SDK is used
- **One `ClineCore`**, created lazily in **local backend mode**
  (`ClineCore.create({ clientName: "hintlab", backendMode: "local" })`) and subscribed once;
  reused across sessions.
- **Start + send:** the first turn is
  `cline.start({ interactive: true, prompt, config: {...}, toolPolicies, capabilities })`;
  follow-up hint levels use `cline.send({ sessionId, prompt })`.
- **Tool policies** (`toolPolicies()` in `src/agent.ts`): `run_commands`, `editor`,
  `apply_patch`, `fetch_web_content`, `skills`, `ask_question`, `submit_and_exit` are
  `{ enabled: false }`; `read_files`, `search_codebase`, `give_hint`, `run_tests` are
  auto-approved.
- **Approval** (`capabilities().requestToolApproval`): returns `{ approved: false }` for
  everything, so any command attempt is blocked and surfaced as an `approval` (denied)
  event — defence-in-depth on top of the disabled `run_commands` policy.
- **`run_commands` allow-list** (`src/allowlist.ts`): first rejects any command containing
  `; && || ` $ | > & newline CR * ?`, then requires an exact match of the whitelist — only
  `python3 main.py`, `python3 main.py < input-*.txt`, `gcc -Wall -O0 main.c -o main`,
  `./main`, `./main < input-*.txt`, and `cat (main.py|main.c|tests.json|input-*.txt)`. Since
  `run_commands` runs **on the host**, this allow-list (plus the disabled policy) is the only
  protection between the model and an arbitrary shell.
- **Custom tools:** `give_hint` and `run_tests` are built with `createTool(...)` + zod
  schemas and passed through `config.extraTools`. `give_hint` is the only hint sink (the
  server-side guard runs inside its `execute`); `run_tests` runs student code through the
  hardened server runner instead of the host shell.
- **Events:** `cline.subscribe(handleCoreEvent)` maps SDK `agent_event`s (tool starts/ends,
  done, error) and `status`/`ended` to the SSE allow-list; model text/reasoning are dropped.
- **Hint guard** (`src/hintGuard.ts`): rejects a hint containing a fenced code block, inline
  code beyond a short identifier, or any line that looks like source code (control flow,
  function calls, assignments, casts, indexing/slicing, comparisons, trailing semicolons).
  A rejected hint becomes a tool error so the model rephrases without code.
- **Sandboxed runner** (`src/runner.ts`): a fresh temp dir per run, per-test timeouts,
  `detached:true` + process-group `SIGKILL` to reap child processes, a minimal env (`PATH`,
  `HOME`=sandbox, `LANG`) so student code cannot see server env or `~/.cline`, signal
  reporting (`SIGSEGV`, `SIGABRT`, …), and cleanup of the temp dir (except the agent's
  workdir, which is removed later at TTL).

### SDK quirks worth knowing
1. **Node 22+** — the SDK and `package.json` `engines` require it.
2. **`moduleResolution: "Bundler"`** (with `module: "ESNext"`) — required by the SDK's type
   exports (`tsconfig.json`).
3. **`read_files` needs absolute paths** — the prompt builder injects
   `path.resolve(sandboxDir, ...)`.
4. **`send()` follow-ups only work after an `interactive: true` `start()`** —
   `src/agent.ts` always starts interactively.
5. **`run_commands` runs on the host** — so the allow-list + disabled policy is the only
   protection; that's why the agent's own test execution goes through the custom `run_tests`
   tool instead.

## 8. Assignments

Each assignment is a directory under `assignments/<id>/` containing a `tests.json` and a
starter source file. `id` is the directory name and must be a "plain slug"
(`^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$` — lowercase letters/digits separated by single hyphens).

`tests.json` shape:

```json
{
  "assignmentId": "sum-of-list",
  "language": "python",
  "statement": "Read space-separated integers on one line and print their sum.",
  "run": "python3 main.py",
  "build": "gcc -Wall -O0 main.c -o main",
  "tests": [
    { "name": "basic", "input": "1 2 3\n", "expected": "6" }
  ]
}
```

- `language`: `"python"` or `"c"`.
- `run`: the command that runs the program; `build` (optional, C only): the compile command.
- Each test: `name` (unique), `input` (fed to stdin verbatim), `expected` (compared to
  trimmed stdout).

The starter file is `main.py` (Python) or `main.c` (C) and is loaded into the editor as the
pre-filled buggy code. To add an assignment, create `assignments/<id>/{tests.json,
main.py|main.c}`; `listAssignments()` discovers it automatically and the runner reads it
fresh per session.

## 9. Troubleshooting

- **`node` too old / `npm install` fails** — the SDK needs Node ≥ 22. `node --version`; install
  Node 22+ (see §1).
- **Missing `gcc` or `python3`** — `test:runner` and the C assignment need them.
  `gcc --version`, `python3 --version`. macOS: `xcode-select --install`. Debian/Ubuntu:
  `sudo apt install -y build-essential python3`. Fedora: `sudo dnf install -y gcc python3`.
- **`EADDRINUSE` / "port already in use"** — another process holds the port. Use
  `PORT=3200 npm start`, or find it: `lsof -i :3000` (macOS) / `ss -ltnp` (Linux), then
  `kill <pid>`. The bundled checks use `PORT=3200` and manage their own server.
- **"Tutor timed out" / no hint appears** — a model call was slow or ClinePass expired. Check
  the feed and server log. The per-turn timeout is `AGENT_TURN_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 5 min).
- **ClinePass not logged in / expired** — `cline config` shows the current provider; re-run
  `cline auth cline-pass`. Without valid credentials the agent turns end in an `error` event.
- **`cline: command not found`** — the CLI isn't on PATH; run `npm install -g cline` and make
  sure npm's global bin (e.g. `~/.npm-global/bin`) is on `PATH`.
- **A hint is rejected and the tutor rephrases** — normal: the model proposed a code-bearing
  hint and the guard made it rephrase; you'll see `hint_rejected` in the feed.

## 10. Project layout

```
HintLab/
├── README.md
├── PLAN.md                  # build plan (aspirational; the code is the source of truth)
├── package.json             # deps + scripts; engines.node >= 22
├── tsconfig.json            # ESNext + moduleResolution Bundler
├── .gitignore               # node_modules, dist, .env, *.log, *.tmp
├── assignments/
│   ├── sum-of-list/{tests.json, main.py}
│   ├── is-palindrome/{tests.json, main.py}
│   └── average-marks/{tests.json, main.c}
├── src/
│   ├── server.ts            # bootstrap: createApp, cleanup loop, listen
│   ├── app.ts               # express routes + static web/
│   ├── config.ts            # env (PORT, timeouts, provider/model)
│   ├── types.ts             # shared TS types
│   ├── assignments.ts       # discover/load/validate tests.json
│   ├── runner.ts            # sandboxed build+run+compare (Python & C)
│   ├── agent.ts             # ClineCore agent (policies, allow-list, give_hint, run_tests)
│   ├── allowlist.ts         # run_commands allow-list
│   ├── hintGuard.ts         # server-side hint guard
│   ├── eventFilter.ts       # SSE allow-list + sanitisation
│   ├── sessions.ts          # in-memory sessions + event bus + TTL cleanup
│   └── sse.ts               # SSE helpers
├── scripts/
│   ├── check-runner.ts      # sandboxed runner checks (no model)
│   ├── check-agent.ts       # allow-list/hint-guard units + real-model e2e
│   └── check-web.ts         # static UI + SSE contract + real-model session
├── web/
│   ├── index.html
│   ├── style.css
│   └── app.js               # vanilla JS UI (EventSource SSE client)
└── cline-proof/             # prompts + session logs + test fixtures (see below)
```

## 11. How this was built

All application code was written by the **Cline CLI** from the prompts in
`cline-proof/prompts/`, with the full session logs in `cline-proof/sessions/` (and in the
Cline session history). The git commits follow the prompt steps (`00-plan`,
`01-server-runner`, `02-agent`, `02c-runner-hardening`, `03-web-ui`).

## 12. Disclosure

- Example Cline SDK snippets (in the now-removed `cline-proof/reference/sdk-check/`) were
  prepared **before** the sprint and used only as reference material for Cline's SDK API.
  They were never imported by the app and were removed from the repo during the sprint (they
  remain in git history). All app code was written by Cline during the sprint, as shown in
  `cline-proof/` (prompts and session logs) and the Cline session history.
- The three sample buggy programs and their `tests.json` files under
  `cline-proof/reference/fixtures/` were prepared **before** the sprint as test data, and
  were copied unchanged into `assignments/`.

1 | # HintLab
  2 | 
  3 | HintLab is a debugging tutor for programming labs. A student picks an assignment (or
  4 | pastes their own program), the server runs the code against the assignment's test cases
  5 | in a sandboxed temporary directory, and then a Cline-SDK agent diagnoses the failures
  6 | and delivers **tiered hints** — level 1 (a conceptual nudge), level 2 (where to look),
  7 | level 3 (the underlying concept) — streamed live to the browser. It is an Express +
  8 | TypeScript server (ESM, run via `tsx`), a vanilla-JS web UI (no build step), and an agent
  9 | built on `@cline/sdk`'s `ClineCore`.
 10 | 
 11 | **Safety promise:** the tutor only diagnoses and hints. It **never** writes or reveals
 12 | the fix. File-editing and network tools are disabled at the SDK policy level, the host
 13 | shell command tool is replaced by a hardened `run_tests` tool and gated by a strict
 14 | allow-list, and every hint is checked by a server-side guard before it reaches the
 15 | student. Model free text and reasoning are filtered out on the server, so only a small
 16 | allow-list of sanitised events ever reaches the browser.
 17 | 
 18 | ## 1. Prerequisites
 19 | 
 20 | | Tool | Version | Why |
 21 | |------|---------|-----|
 22 | | Node.js | **22 or newer** (the Cline SDK and `package.json` `engines` both require `>=22`) | runtime + SDK |
 23 | | npm | bundled with Node | install |
 24 | | Python 3 | `python3` on PATH | runs the Python assignments and `test:runner` |
 25 | | C compiler | `gcc` (on macOS the `gcc`/`cc` shim from Xcode Command Line Tools — i.e. Apple clang — works) | compiles the C assignment |
 26 | | git | any recent | clone |
 27 | | Cline CLI (`cline`) | latest (verified on `3.0.68`) | only for real model calls (`check:agent`, `check:web`, and actually using the tutor) |
 28 | | `pgrep` | any | used by `npm run test:runner` to assert process-group cleanup (built in on macOS; `procps` on Linux) |
 29 | 
 30 | Check what you have:
 31 | 
 32 | ```sh
 33 | node --version      # must be v22+ (verified v24.16.0)
 34 | npm --version
 35 | python3 --version
 36 |  gcc --version       # macOS: Apple clang …; Linux: gcc (…)
 37 | git --version

 73 | ## 2. Cline CLI + ClinePass (provider credentials)
 74 | 
 75 | HintLab does **not** ship or read an API key. In local backend mode the SDK resolves
 76 | credentials itself from the Cline CLI's config directory (`~/.cline`), so the only setup
 77 | step is to install the CLI and authenticate it with ClinePass once.
 78 | 
 79 | 1. Install the CLI (installs the `cline` binary):
 80 | 
 81 |    ```sh
 82 |    npm install -g cline
 83 |    cline --version      # verified on 3.0.68
 84 |    ```
 85 | 
 86 | 2. Authenticate with ClinePass. `cline auth` takes a positional provider shorthand and
 87 |    flags (`-p/--provider`, `-k/--apikey`, `-m/--modelid`, `-b/--baseurl`):
 88 | 
 89 |    ```sh
 90 |    cline auth --help
 91 |    # Usage: cline auth [options] [provider]
 92 |    #   provider              Provider id (positional shorthand for -p)
 93 |    #   -p, --provider <id>   Provider ID
 94 |    #   -k, --apikey <key>    API key
 95 |    #   -m, --modelid <id>    Model ID

100 |    ```

168 | 
169 | 1. Pick **`sum-of-list`** from the drop-down. The statement ("Read space-separated
170 |    integers on one line and print their sum.") appears and the buggy starter is preloaded

183 | ## 5. npm scripts and checks
184 | 
185 | | Script | Command | What it does |
186 | |--------|---------|--------------|
187 | | `npm start` | `tsx src/server.ts` | Run the server once |

224 | ## 6. API reference
225 | 
226 | Base URL `http://localhost:3000` (or your `PORT`).
227 | 
228 | ### `GET /api/health`
229 | - `200` → `{ "status": "ok" }`
230 | 
231 | ### `GET /api/assignments`
232 | - `200` → array of `{ id, language, statement, starterCode }` for each discovered assignment.
233 | 
234 | ### `POST /api/session`
235 | Run a submission and start a background level-1 agent turn.
236 | - Request body: `{ "assignmentId": "sum-of-list", "code": "…" }` — `code` is optional
237 |   (omitted / empty / `null` uses the starter code).
238 | - `200` → `{ "sessionId": "<uuid>", "testResults": { assignmentId, build, tests[], passed, failed, total } }`
239 |   (`testResults` is the sanitised shape below — no `sandboxDir`, trimmed `stderr`).
240 | - Errors: `400` (body not an object, missing/bad `assignmentId`, `code` not a string),
241 |   `404` (unknown `assignmentId`), `500` (internal error).
242 | 
243 | ### `GET /api/session/:id/stream`
244 | Server-Sent Events. `200`/`text/event-stream`; `404` if the session is unknown. Replays the
245 | buffered events, then streams live ones, with `: ping` heartbeats.
246 | 
247 | ### `POST /api/session/:id/next-hint`
248 | Ask for the next hint level (2, then 3).
249 | - `200` → `{ "level": 2, "status": "idle" }` — the hint itself arrives over SSE. After all
250 |   three hints: `{ "level": 3, "status": "complete", "message": "All three hint levels have already been delivered." }`.
251 | - Errors: `404` unknown session, `409` agent still busy.
252 | 
253 | ### Static
254 | `GET /` and the `web/` assets are served with `express.static`.
255 | 
256 | ### SSE event types that reach the client
257 | 
258 | Only the types below are ever forwarded; everything else (including the model's free text
259 | and reasoning) is dropped by `src/eventFilter.ts`.
260 | 
261 | | Event | Payload |
262 | |-------|---------|
263 | | `test_results` | `{ assignmentId, build: { ok, timedOut, signal, stderr } \| null, tests: [{ name, input, expected, got, stderr, exitCode, signal, timedOut, passed }], passed, failed, total }` |
264 | | `tool_call` | `run_commands` → `{ toolName, command }`; `read_files` → `{ toolName, file }`; `run_tests` → `{ toolName, testName }` |
265 | | `tool_result` | `run_commands` → `{ toolName, output }`; `run_tests` → `{ toolName, passed, failed, total, build, tests[] }` (`read_files` results are dropped — they would leak the student's code) |
266 | | `approval` | `{ toolName, command, allowed, reason? }` (in HintLab `allowed` is always `false`) |
267 | | `hint` | `{ level, tag, text }` |
268 | | `hint_rejected` | `{ level, reason }` with `reason` ∈ `"wrong level" \| "empty hint" \| "contained code"` (never the rejected text) |
269 | | `hint_status` | whitelisted (reserved); the server currently emits `hint_rejected` instead |
270 | | `status` | `{ status }` — `created`, `running`, `idle`, `complete`, `error` |
271 | | `error` | `{ message }` — a short friendly line, never a stack trace or SDK text |
272 | | `done` | `{ reason }` |
273 | 
274 | **Filtering:** raw agent events (`agent_text`, `reasoning`, unguarded tool output) are
275 | recorded server-side for debugging but never streamed; `filterEvent` applies the allow-list
276 | and sanitisation to both live events and the replayed history, so late joiners get the same
277 | contract.
278 | 
279 | ## 7. Architecture
280 | 
281 | ```
282 |  Browser (web/index.html + app.js — vanilla JS, EventSource)
283 |    │  POST /api/session  { assignmentId, code }
284 |    ▼
285 |  Express + TS server (src/app.ts, src/server.ts)          ESM, run via tsx
286 |    │
287 |    ├─ runAssignment(...,{cleanup:false}) ──► sandbox runner (src/runner.ts)
288 |    │     fresh temp dir os.tmpdir()/hintlab-<uuid>
289 |    │     writes main.py/main.c + tests.json + input-<name>.txt
290 |    │     build (gcc) / run (python3|./main) with per-test timeout,
291 |    │     process-group kill, minimal env (PATH, HOME=sandbox, LANG)
292 |    │
293 |    ├─ startSession / nextHint ──► ClineCore agent (src/agent.ts)
294 |    │     ClineCore.create({ clientName:"hintlab", backendMode:"local" })   (once, lazy)
295 |    │     cline.start({ interactive:true, prompt, config:{sessionId, providerId, modelId,
296 |    │                   temperature:0, systemPrompt, cwd, workspaceRoot, enableTools,
297 |    │                   enableSpawnAgent:false, enableAgentTeams:false, extraTools},
298 |    │                   toolPolicies, capabilities })
299 |    │     cline.send({ sessionId, prompt })   for the next hint
300 |    │     cline.subscribe(handleCoreEvent)    ->  mapped to SSE events
301 |    │     give_hint (createTool + zod)  +  run_tests (createTool + zod)  via extraTools
302 |    │
303 |    ├─ GET  /api/session/:id/stream  (SSE)  ◄── eventFilter.ts allow-list + sanitisation
304 |    └─ POST /api/session/:id/next-hint
305 | ```
306 | 
307 | ### How the SDK is used
308 | - **One `ClineCore`**, created lazily in **local backend mode**
309 |   (`ClineCore.create({ clientName: "hintlab", backendMode: "local" })`) and subscribed once;
310 |   reused across sessions.
311 | - **Start + send:** the first turn is
312 |   `cline.start({ interactive: true, prompt, config: {...}, toolPolicies, capabilities })`;
313 |   follow-up hint levels use `cline.send({ sessionId, prompt })`.
314 | - **Tool policies** (`toolPolicies()` in `src/agent.ts`): `run_commands`, `editor`,
315 |   `apply_patch`, `fetch_web_content`, `skills`, `ask_question`, `submit_and_exit` are
316 |   `{ enabled: false }`; `read_files`, `search_codebase`, `give_hint`, `run_tests` are
317 |   auto-approved.
318 | - **Approval** (`capabilities().requestToolApproval`): returns `{ approved: false }` for
319 |   everything, so any command attempt is blocked and surfaced as an `approval` (denied)
320 |   event — defence-in-depth on top of the disabled `run_commands` policy.
321 | - **`run_commands` allow-list** (`src/allowlist.ts`): first rejects any command containing
322 |   `; && || ` $ | > & newline CR * ?`, then requires an exact match of the whitelist — only
323 |   `python3 main.py`, `python3 main.py < input-*.txt`, `gcc -Wall -O0 main.c -o main`,
324 |   `./main`, `./main < input-*.txt`, and `cat (main.py|main.c|tests.json|input-*.txt)`. Since
325 |   `run_commands` runs **on the host**, this allow-list (plus the disabled policy) is the only
326 |   protection between the model and an arbitrary shell.
327 | - **Custom tools:** `give_hint` and `run_tests` are built with `createTool(...)` + zod
328 |   schemas and passed through `config.extraTools`. `give_hint` is the only hint sink (the
329 |   server-side guard runs inside its `execute`); `run_tests` runs student code through the
330 |   hardened server runner instead of the host shell.
331 | - **Events:** `cline.subscribe(handleCoreEvent)` maps SDK `agent_event`s (tool starts/ends,
332 |   done, error) and `status`/`ended` to the SSE allow-list; model text/reasoning are dropped.
333 | - **Hint guard** (`src/hintGuard.ts`): rejects a hint containing a fenced code block, inline
334 |   code beyond a short identifier, or any line that looks like source code (control flow,
335 |   function calls, assignments, casts, indexing/slicing, comparisons, trailing semicolons).
336 |   A rejected hint becomes a tool error so the model rephrases without code.
337 | - **Sandboxed runner** (`src/runner.ts`): a fresh temp dir per run, per-test timeouts,
338 |   `detached:true` + process-group `SIGKILL` to reap child processes, a minimal env (`PATH`,
339 |   `HOME`=sandbox, `LANG`) so student code cannot see server env or `~/.cline`, signal
340 |   reporting (`SIGSEGV`, `SIGABRT`, …), and cleanup of the temp dir (except the agent's
341 |   workdir, which is removed later at TTL).
342 | 
343 | ### SDK quirks worth knowing
344 | 1. **Node 22+** — the SDK and `package.json` `engines` require it.
345 | 2. **`moduleResolution: "Bundler"`** (with `module: "ESNext"`) — required by the SDK's type
346 |    exports (`tsconfig.json`).
347 | 3. **`read_files` needs absolute paths** — the prompt builder injects
348 |    `path.resolve(sandboxDir, ...)`.
349 | 4. **`send()` follow-ups only work after an `interactive: true` `start()`** —
350 |    `src/agent.ts` always starts interactively.
351 | 5. **`run_commands` runs on the host** — so the allow-list + disabled policy is the only
352 |    protection; that's why the agent's own test execution goes through the custom `run_tests`
353 |    tool instead.
354 | 
355 | ## 8. Assignments
356 | 
357 | Each assignment is a directory under `assignments/<id>/` containing a `tests.json` and a
358 | starter source file. `id` is the directory name and must be a "plain slug"
359 | (`^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$` — lowercase letters/digits separated by single hyphens).
360 | 
361 | `tests.json` shape:
362 | 
363 | ```json
364 | {
365 |   "assignmentId": "sum-of-list",
366 |   "language": "python",
367 |   "statement": "Read space-separated integers on one line and print their sum.",
368 |   "run": "python3 main.py",
369 |   "build": "gcc -Wall -O0 main.c -o main",
370 |   "tests": [
371 |     { "name": "basic", "input": "1 2 3\n", "expected": "6" }
372 |   ]
373 | }
374 | ```
375 | 
376 | - `language`: `"python"` or `"c"`.
377 | - `run`: the command that runs the program; `build` (optional, C only): the compile command.
378 | - Each test: `name` (unique), `input` (fed to stdin verbatim), `expected` (compared to
379 |   trimmed stdout).
380 | 
381 | The starter file is `main.py` (Python) or `main.c` (C) and is loaded into the editor as the
382 | pre-filled buggy code. To add an assignment, create `assignments/<id>/{tests.json,
383 | main.py|main.c}`; `listAssignments()` discovers it automatically and the runner reads it
384 | fresh per session.
385 | 
386 | ## 9. Troubleshooting
387 | 
388 | - **`node` too old / `npm install` fails** — the SDK needs Node ≥ 22. `node --version`; install
389 |   Node 22+ (see §1).
390 | - **Missing `gcc` or `python3`** — `test:runner` and the C assignment need them.
391 |   `gcc --version`, `python3 --version`. macOS: `xcode-select --install`. Debian/Ubuntu:
392 |   `sudo apt install -y build-essential python3`. Fedora: `sudo dnf install -y gcc python3`.
393 | - **`EADDRINUSE` / "port already in use"** — another process holds the port. Use
394 |   `PORT=3200 npm start`, or find it: `lsof -i :3000` (macOS) / `ss -ltnp` (Linux), then
395 |   `kill <pid>`. The bundled checks use `PORT=3200` and manage their own server.
396 | - **"Tutor timed out" / no hint appears** — a model call was slow or ClinePass expired. Check
397 |   the feed and server log. The per-turn timeout is `AGENT_TURN_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 5 min).
398 | - **ClinePass not logged in / expired** — `cline config` shows the current provider; re-run
399 |   `cline auth cline-pass`. Without valid credentials the agent turns end in an `error` event.
400 | - **`cline: command not found`** — the CLI isn't on PATH; run `npm install -g cline` and make
401 |   sure npm's global bin (e.g. `~/.npm-global/bin`) is on `PATH`.
402 | - **A hint is rejected and the tutor rephrases** — normal: the model proposed a code-bearing
403 |   hint and the guard made it rephrase; you'll see `hint_rejected` in the feed.
404 |
